## ⚠️ 4 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/7997-detail-view-related-retired.md`

- names `renderers/record-details.tsx` → `packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/record-details.tsx` — edited by this change

  > **Why it retired.** `@objectstack/spec` declares no `DetailView` schema at all — every `DetailView` occurrence in `packages/spec/src` is prose about this repo's own `RecordDetailView.tsx` — so this array mirrored no protocol schema and drifted freely: it declared `columns` as `TableColumn[]` while the renderer it fed also accepted bare field names, `{ field, label }` and legacy `{ name, label }` spellings. The axis that carried the ruling was measured **zero pull**: no application code authored the member, both internal producers of a `detail-view` node (`RecordDetailDrawer`, `renderers/record-details.tsx`) synthesize it without `related`, and the only in-tree authorings carrying real columns were two documents — both rewritten here.

### `.changeset/8400-kanban-name-field-skip-set.md`

- names `record-details.tsx` → `packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/record-details.tsx` — edited by this change

  > Deliberately one rung, unlike the same dedupe in `record-details.tsx`, which also carries `deriveTitleField`: that ladder filters a synthesized field list, whereas this one filters an author-declared `cardFields`, where dropping a field the author asked for is a worse failure than a repeated title. A regression test pins both directions, including an object whose declared and derived pointers disagree.

### `.changeset/8649-detail-renderer-undeclared-keys.md`

- names `record-details.tsx` → `packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/record-details.tsx` — edited by this change

  > **`@object-ui/plugin-detail` — the annotation-erasing destructure default is gone from three renderers.** `record-details.tsx`, `record-highlights.tsx` and `record-related-list.tsx` each annotated `schema` correctly and then wrote `schema = {} as any`. A destructuring default's type joins the annotated property type at the binding, so `any` erased the annotation for *every* read site in the file — declared keys and undeclared ones alike read `any`. No published surface moves: the exported annotations were always correct.

- names `record-highlights.tsx` → `packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/record-highlights.tsx` — edited by this change

  > **`@object-ui/plugin-detail` — the annotation-erasing destructure default is gone from three renderers.** `record-details.tsx`, `record-highlights.tsx` and `record-related-list.tsx` each annotated `schema` correctly and then wrote `schema = {} as any`. A destructuring default's type joins the annotated property type at the binding, so `any` erased the annotation for *every* read site in the file — declared keys and undeclared ones alike read `any`. - names `record-related-list.tsx` → `packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/record-related-list.tsx` — edited by this change

  > **`@object-ui/plugin-detail` — the annotation-erasing destructure default is gone from three renderers.** `record-details.tsx`, `record-highlights.tsx` and `record-related-list.tsx` each annotated `schema` correctly and then wrote `schema = {} as any`. A destructuring default's type joins the annotated property type at the binding, so `any` erased the annotation for *every* read site in the file — declared keys and undeclared ones alike read `any`. No published surface moves: the exported annotations were always correct.

### `.changeset/9280-record-highlights-entry-icon-retired.md`

- names `packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/record-highlights.tsx` → `packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/record-highlights.tsx` — edited by this change

  > - `packages/types/src/record-components.ts` — `RecordHighlightsComponentProps.fields[]`'s object arm: `{ name; label?; icon?; type?; readonly? }` → **`{ name; label?; type?; readonly? }`**. The key is **removed, not tombstoned**: the contract's arm is `$strict`, so the refusal an author needs already exists upstream and arrives named (`invalid_union` at the entry). A `?: never` tombstone buys nothing here — it is the remedy for a non-strict mirror that would otherwise strip in silence, which is not this arm. - `packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/record-highlights.tsx` — the entry normalizer stops copying `icon: f?.icon` into the normalized entry. That read was **unreachable**, not merely unused: no author could feed it past the `$strict` arm, and `HeaderHighlight` renders no `.icon` on the far side either, so the copy had no consumer in either direction. - `packages/plugin-detail/src/index.tsx` — the registry manifest's `fields` input description sketched the entry as `{name,label?,icon?,type?,readonly?}` → **`{name,label?,type?,readonly?}`**. The `inputs` ARE the published contract (`gen-manifest.ts` serializes them into `sdui.manifest.json` and `sdui-intrinsics.d.ts`), so leaving the sketch standing would have gone on teaching AI and human authors a key that gets the whole document refused at publish.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `80c54122e` (merge-base with origin/main): 5 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1248 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (1813 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/35530835997)

## ACCEPT — PR #10164, card objectui#10155

Reviewed by the `domain:ui` execution seat (Seat: domain:ui#2, session `session_018HrVaotisyhgmot9o2MLRq`) at 2026-09-20T18:58Z. `Implemented-by:` an `os-dev` subagent of this session · `Reviewed-by:` this seat. ⛔ Landing held on checks — 11 of 42 pending, 0 failed at this reading.

⚠️ The seat **filed** this card, so its measurements carried no second opinion and the dev was told to re-derive them. It did, and it corrected one of them.

### ⭐ The grade question is closed — with readings, not with a shrug

This card refused to guess whether these blocks' actions are independently refused server-side, because that decides p0 versus p1. The dev read `objectstack-ai/objectstack` and answered it; this seat re-derived all three readings on that repo's `origin/main`:

1. `rest-route-ledger.ts` states of the data-actions family, in capitals, 「**THERE IS NO ACTION-INVOKE ROUTE IN THIS FAMILY, AND ITS ABSENCE IS DELIBERATE**」, with a QA probe recording four candidate spellings answering 404 against a booted showcase.
2. `actionPermissionError` in `packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts` enforces an action's own `requiredPermissions`, called from the runtime dispatcher's `/actions` domain under 「[ADR-0066 D4] Dual-surface action gate — **the server is the source of truth**」 and from the MCP `run_action` bridge. Fail-closed: `new Set(ec?.systemPermissions ?? [])`, only `ec.isSystem` bypasses.
3. The displayed data is admitted by the engine middleware's object-read gate, which `canReadObject`'s docblock describes arm for arm including the ADR-0066 D3 capability AND-gate, and states 「Fails CLOSED.」

⇒ nothing on these surfaces is authorised by the client gate. **p1 holds, ⛔ not p0.** This also closes the question PR objectui#10153 parked hours ago as 「reported unanswered rather than guessed」 — ⭐ the right call then, and this is the reading it was waiting for.

⭐ The edge the dev volunteered rather than smoothed over: `actionPermissionError` returns `null` for an action declaring no capabilities, so the **block-level** key alone never had server backing. It does not move the grade — a client gate was never an authorisation — and a report that surfaces the fact working against its own tidy conclusion is worth more than one that does not.

### One of this seat's own relayed claims, corrected

The card said `record-related-list.tsx` 「does not even carry the `objectName` guard the others have」. **True as written; it implies something false.** Verified here: that site's `objectName` is `schema.objectName` and the missing-objectName placeholder returns **before** the gate — the module's docblock records that `ElementDataSourceGate` maps `object` onto `objectName` before the body ever sees it. ⇒ ⛔ no fail-open from the absent conjunct there. Corrected on the card too.

### The pin-file disease check, asked for and actually run

⭐ Only `record-details.test.tsx` had any pin naming this key, and it **did** carry the disease PR objectui#10153 found — `usePermissions: () => ({ can: () => stub.can })`, a `can`-stub with no `hasCapabilities`, i.e. a pin that would pass on the defect. Its subject is the rules-of-hooks contract rather than the gate, so it was **repaired** rather than rewritten, and its docblock now says it pins nothing about the gate's semantics. `record-highlights` and `record-related-list` had **no** pin on this key in any file — nothing to extend, which is its own answer about how this family went unnoticed.

46 new pins in one harness over all three blocks, every one mounting a **real** provider; the only double is a delegating `can`/`cannot` spy that changes no answer.

### ⭐ The ablation is reported AS MEASURED, and two legs did not match the template

25 red / 24 green, with the three renderers restored to their base blobs verified on disk by `git hash-object`, a trap holding absolute restore paths, and the on-disk text counted both ways per file (capability-gate 1 → 0, object-action-gate 0 → 1). The 24 green are the controls — **including both `can()` truth tables**, which is the evidence they pin `can()` and not this gate.

Two legs deviated and the dev said so instead of quietly adjusting the expectation:

- the role-based WITH-config leg went red on **2 of 3** blocks, because `record:related_list` reads its **child** object, which carries no config in either arm of that pair — so pre-fix it answered the same either way;
- related-list's DISCRIMINATOR ② could not be given hostile object bits at all, because its own automatic object-read gate refuses an `allowRead: false` object one branch earlier. It is pinned on `allowRead: true`, and the `allowRead: false` leg is pinned separately **as the object-read call this card must not move**.

⭐ An ablation whose legs are reported where they landed rather than where a template predicted is the difference between evidence and decoration.

### Clause-② — `no`, and the ⛔ defect in the carrier was this seat's

`--pair 10164` first exited **4**: this seat's claim comment carried the key **mid-line**, inside the sentence that deliberately deferred the value, and that limb is read line-anchored. Repaired by the `Clause-②-correction:` comment naming that claim. ⛔ The dev correctly declined to post it — the carrier is the claiming seat's act, and the script says in terms that a checker must not fill the line in on the seat's behalf. `--pair 10164` now exits **0**; `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr objectstack-ai/objectui#10164` exits **0**.

⛔ `needs:contract-review` is not hung, and this seat's judgement agrees with the dev's reading: the diff touches only `packages/plugin-detail/src` and `.changeset`, adds no export, no schema key, no closed-set member and no registry entry.

### Also answered rather than ignored

All four are, checked one by one — two are untouched by this diff, the annotation-erasing-destructure one still holds (all three renderers still spell the `NonNullable` form, no `as any` reintroduced), and the highlights-normalizer one still holds (the normalizer is untouched).
